chunks: From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'I heard God saying, "God destroys usury and increases charity." Yet I see those who consume usury seeing their wealth increase.' He said, 'What destruction is greater than a dirham of usury that destroys the religion? And even if he repents from it, his wealth will be lost and he will become poor.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to the wealth of someone who consumes usury even if they repent?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the paradox of usury by distinguishing between apparent material accumulation and the actual spiritual erosion of faith (din), noting that even repentance does not restore the specific wealth acquired through riba. This hadith, found in Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, underscores the Shia scholarly view that riba causes a fundamental 'drying up' of divine blessing, leading to eventual poverty despite outward prosperity. It serves as a critical ethical warning for merchants, linking financial transactions directly to spiritual integrity.
